title: Freeze independent evidence and test infrastructure
dependencies: None; start from the attached baseline
addresses: Handoff C1-C5; additional D1 first-cluster corruption and D2 WAV private seek state; all subsequent acceptance machinery.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 1, 4, 10 and 14; src/Makefile.am; test/Makefile.am; dsf.c; dsdiff.c; formats.c; wav.c; evidence/probe_io.c and reproduce.py.
existing: Makefile.am, src/Makefile.am and test/Makefile.am only as needed to register maintainer/test targets.
new: tests/dsd/{fixtures,reference,results}; tests/dsd/run.py; tests/dsd/measure.py; tests/dsd/bench.py; tests/dsd/test_io.c; docs/dsd/BASELINE.md.
steps: Install the approved design/plan/SOW overlay under docs/dsd. Record source and toolchain hashes. Build the untouched baseline. Generate hand-derived tiny DSF/DFF/DoP vectors and independent chunk walking. Port the supplied reproductions into explicit named xfails. Establish deterministic seeds, JSON result schemas, CPU/build metadata and a throughput harness. Add test modes that later phases can extend rather than creating a separate runner per phase.
unit: Fixture generator self-tests; independently checked bit chronology; chunk spans; exact integer count helpers in the harness; xfail classification that fails if the expected defect disappears or changes unexpectedly.
integration: Reproduce small reads, MSB rejection, first DFF cluster under allocator perturbation, odd/tail chunk defects, multichannel seek, MANF, DSF Type 5 loss and WAV rewind after manual core-position correction. Run existing make check.
numerical: Implement measurement definitions and data schemas, not new acceptance claims. Record filter feasibility as supplied evidence only. Prepare analysis-v1 generation entry point and synthetic PCM source fixtures.
bench: Record native transcode and direct ultra-quality decode baselines for DSD64/128/256, 1/2/6 channels, including 352.8/705.6 kHz; a short development matrix is acceptable here if full commands and durations are stored.
done: Untouched behavior still reproduces each named defect; generic tests pass; make check-dsd succeeds with only enumerated baseline xfails; all logs identify actual executed commands.
risks: Accidentally using the writer under test as the fixture oracle; blanket xfails; host-specific timings mistaken for universal results.
outscope: Production fixes, new DSP, new defaults, ISA optimization and full proprietary/hardware validation.
contract: The repository is commit 16aa7e17531dd3612f29247da98c8ea570cd905a. Do not alter production behavior. Public SoX I/O counts interleaved samples; fixture truth must distinguish chronological per-channel frames. Preserve a known failing test for each defect, including the newly demonstrated first DFF byte and WAV counter defects. A test being skipped is not a pass.

title: Repair DSDIFF output structure and first-cluster bits
addresses: C1.1-C1.4 and additional confirmed defect D1.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 1.2 and 4.1; src/dsdiff.c dff_writeheader/startwrite/write_bits/write_buf/stopwrite; tests/dsd writer fixtures.
existing: src/dsdiff.c; test registration only if needed.
new: Focused writer regression vectors and chunk-walker expected structures in tests/dsd.
steps: Zero the initial byte-cluster accumulator. Define checked physical span(n)=12+n+(n&1). Correct FRM8/PROP size accumulation. Use CMPR name length 14 and payload length 19 with external pad. Count a silence-completed final cluster in audio size. Write external audio padding without counting it as audio. Preserve the existing 0x69 chronological completion convention and propagate write/seek failures.
unit: Size arithmetic; CMPR count/payload; initial accumulator; partial final cluster for each residual bit count 1..7.
integration: Independent walker over empty, one-byte, even/odd and multichannel files; byte-for-byte program payload under allocator perturbation; original generic suite; cross-format chronology with expected DFF completion.
numerical: No DSP changes. Assert native source bits remain identical through their logical endpoint; DFF logical output rounds up to eight frames only when completion is required.
bench: Native DFF writing at 1/2/6 channels versus P00; reject a repeatable regression beyond the unchanged-path tolerance.
done: All C1/D1 xfails become hard passes; first output bits do not depend on allocator contents; declared and physical spans agree for every fixture.
risks: Counting a pad as sound; completing one byte instead of one byte per channel; arithmetic fixes concealing an incorrect physical file.
outscope: Reader redesign, seek fixes, channel metadata, DSP, automatic mode and ISA changes.
contract: This is a localized DFF writer patch. A nine-frame mono source becomes sixteen DFF frames because DFF has byte-granular duration; the last seven are the existing explicit completion pattern. That is not a reason to corrupt the first nine. Never reintroduce payload double counting or count CMPR NUL as text.

title: Make DSD readers retained-bit streaming state machines
addresses: C3, C4; tiny/empty valid files; shared DFF/WSD state constraints; DoP capacity invariance if its API probe exposes a defect.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 2.2, 4.2 and 4.5; src/dsf.c; src/dsdiff.c; src/dop.c; P00 small-capacity tests.
existing: src/dsf.c; src/dsdiff.c; src/dop.c only for an independently tested capacity correction.
new: Small-read, bit-order, zero-capacity and parser extent tests in tests/dsd.
steps: Retain byte/block/bit position across calls. Load a DFF/WSD byte cluster only when the cached cluster is exhausted. Make one-frame capacity progress. Accept DSF bps 1 and 8 with normalization outside the hot bit loop. Remove the invalid eight-byte DFF minimum; require complete channel clusters. Handle zero logical frames explicitly. Initialize required parser fields and validate enclosing spans/skip results. Add no duplicate DFF remaining-audio counter. Check DoP pending output before writing to a zero-capacity destination.
unit: Capacities 0 and 1..17 frames; bytes with asymmetric reversal patterns; tails 1..7 bits; cache invalidation; mandatory-field/extent initialization.
integration: Channels 1..6 including CLI --buffer 32; multiple DSF blocks; mono one-byte DFF; forward-only streams where supported; baseline DoP hand vectors and backpressure.
numerical: Concatenated small-read output equals the independent large-read chronological reference exactly. No DSP or level change.
bench: Small/large-buffer native reads and native transcodes; retained state must not cause a large-read throughput regression outside the specified tolerance.
done: C3/C4 xfails become hard passes; no legal positive whole-frame read returns false EOF; all source-order forms yield identical chronology.
risks: Decoding a fresh cluster over a partially consumed one; treating numeric zero as a DSD silence bit; accepting malformed extents as a substitute for proper empty-file handling.
outscope: Core seek bookkeeping, new layout model, reconstruction filters, SDM selection and speculative WSD speaker mapping.
contract: Public read capacity is interleaved samples, rounded down to a complete channel frame. A request for one frame means channels samples, not one byte per channel. DSF bps=8 is MSB-first one-bit DSD, not 8-bit PCM. A cache is justified streaming state; a second remaining-audio counter for the old MANF symptom is not.

title: Unify seek units and reset logical and private positions

new: Seek-handler inventory; unit conversion helper tests; optional-codec fixtures/tests; docs/dsd/SEEK_CONTRACT.md.
steps: Normalize offset down to a complete channel frame once in core. Check known bounds and arithmetic. On successful seek commit olength to normalized interleaved target. Clamp known-length reads without unsigned underflow. Normalize native handlers to per-channel positions and clear caches. Reset WAV numSamples from original total; implement exact GSM block seek plus discard or return unsupported. Correct interactive callers and only update their counters on success. Verify pending FLAC seeks cannot leak old buffered samples.
unit: Aligned and unaligned public offsets; byte/non-byte DSD positions; end and out-of-range seeks; multiplication overflow; pending cache state; failure before physical movement.
integration: Read-rewind-read, seek after prior reads, DFF MANF, sequential versus seek-optimized native trim; WAV PCM and GSM, raw PCM and available optional codecs; channels 1..6.
numerical: Exact slice equality and remaining frame counts. No filter, gain or encoder changes.
bench: Seek latency and sequential read throughput versus P00; no per-sample generic overhead beyond bounded remaining-length checks.
done: Every successful built-in seek in the audited set resolves to the normalized target; C2/D2 cases pass; optional dependency gaps are named, not inferred passed.
risks: Assigning olength while a decoder lands elsewhere; double channel multiplication; fixing core but leaving WAV private state stale.
outscope: SEEK_CUR/END, a general random-access decoder redesign, DFF-private MANF counters and DSP pre-roll optimization.
contract: sox_seek offsets remain interleaved samples. For compatibility, floor an unaligned request to its containing whole frame and document it. Exact-end seek is valid. A DFF MANF over-read is resolved by core position and correct native units; WAV independently needs its private remaining counter reset. Do not merge these root causes or pretend one assignment fixes both.

title: Preserve DSD channel identity with bounded metadata APIs

DSF cannot truthfully encode an arbitrary unknown layout. A float WAV file still needs a correct speaker mask; its encoding does not solve channel semantics.

title: Implement the DSD contract and preflight domain planner
addresses: Explicit native/PCM/DoP boundary; pre-combiner scaling/mixing; headers before effects; retained DSD reference level; versioned rate/profile descriptors and CLI policy.

steps: Implement exact native rate capabilities with 512/1024 disabled. Parse and validate the specified options/effect configurations. Produce immutable plans before open_output_file. Keep native and effective per-input signals separate. Classify unknown effects as PCM and unknown multichannel layout transforms conservatively. Resolve working rates, reference-level tags/inverse decoder gain for remodulation, explicit rate semantics, transport requirements, clip/layout policies and trim optimization eligibility without starting effects twice. Emit inspectable plan JSON for tests.

Input volume and parallel combination require per-input reconstruction before balance_input; adding an effect after the combiner is too late. A leading ordinary rate operates on reconstructed PCM and retains its options. This phase establishes plans, not a claim that unimplemented DSP already works.

title: Generate certified filters and implement scalar reconstruction

Implement per-channel rings, factor-two phases, scalar symmetric kernels and bounded streaming. Use candidate tap sequences 57x4+117, 57x4+153, 57x5+117 and 57x4+257, increasing only with documented regenerated evidence. Align phase G mod D and discard floor(G/D). Produce centered intermediate samples with the specified finite zero-extension policy.

bench: Scalar kernel and front-end throughput/memory for 64/128/256, 1/2/6 channels; record tap-count costs without claiming SIMD speedup.
done: Coefficient bytes, mathematical oracles, stream endpoints and scalar response all pass; candidate feasibility files are not blindly promoted as certificates.
risks: Confusing stage input rate with output rate; last-stage-only alias testing; wrong fractional phase; numeric zero versus a DSD zero bit.
outscope: Arbitrary-ratio SRC, automatic CLI routing, encoder profiles, SIMD and higher native-rate enablement.
contract: Mastering P/S/R in Hz: 64=20000/40000/88200; 128=30000/60000/176400; 256=40000/80000/176400. Wideband R=Fs/32, P=.4R, S=.5R. All are linear phase and unity DC. Scalar output uses binary64. Finite boundaries are numeric zero outside the input, not 0x69 or all-zero DSD bits. No new arbitrary-ratio resampler is authorized.

title: Integrate the private double SRC and explicit dsdpcm effect
addresses: All nine PCM outputs through 705.6 kHz; one final quantization; exact composite counts; level/headroom behavior.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 3.3-3.4 and 6.4-6.6; src/rate.c backend and public wrapper; effects.c flow cloning; src/dsd_decode.c.

steps: Expose an opaque binary64 wrapper around the existing static rate backend without altering the public effect. Use linear phase, rejection 180 and 95-percent 0-dB bandwidth, equivalent to -B not -b. Implement explicit zero-extension and caller-controlled final frame limits. Compose reconstruction with final SRC. Add public multichannel decoder and a mono-per-flow dsdpcm adapter. Apply preserve or exact gain two once, then explicit graph clipping policy. Add the private fatal status so strict clipping stops before a failed block is interleaved/emitted; latch details, preserve normal EOF semantics and make CLI exit/finalization status truthful.
unit: Identity SRC; rational count arithmetic; tiny streams and double-rounding counterexamples; finish with needed extra support; separate contexts and per-channel ownership; API overrange values.
integration: Explicit dsdpcm across 3x9x2 matrix; buffer/thread invariance; float output still graph-clipped in CLI; clipping warnings/errors including mono/multichannel fatal flow/drain and a following chain; finalization failure; strict versus adapt bandwidth; legacy public rate regression goldens.
numerical: Full impulse/phase/endpoint and response envelope; independent final-SRC reference at 48 kHz-family ratios; <=1 int32 LSB scalar/vector-ready FIR-boundary tolerance; exact output counts.
bench: Explicit decode throughput and memory, especially master64->705600 and wide256->705600, versus direct and bandwidth-matched staged controls.
done: All explicit conversions work to 705.6 kHz; public rate behavior remains unchanged; no false claim that float output bypasses int32 graph limits.
risks: Inheriting legacy LPC extrapolation accidentally; rounding intermediate length twice; owning pointers allocated before effect cloning; using -b as a 0-dB bandwidth.
outscope: Automatic input adapters/defaults, new encoder selection, ISA specialization and a direct floating CLI writer pipeline.
contract: Pure conversion count is floor(Nnative*Fout/Fnative+1/2), computed with checked integer arithmetic. Generate ceil(N/D) intermediate samples, zero-extend that finite sequence for the final SRC, and return only the original-timebase final count. Preserve is unity; sacd is exactly gain two. Double API values may exceed one; ordinary SoX graph samples cannot.

Apply known file gain to binary64 reconstructed PCM before graph quantization and suppress duplicate balance_input gain. Carry DSD-origin calibration into planned remodulation. Insert explicit/automatic boundaries once. Preserve native repacking and DoP. Disable native trim seek optimization in reconstructed chains until context-aware parity exists. Enforce downstream-domain constraints and headers/layout before audio. Keep encoder automatic promotion unavailable until P10/P15, with a clear interim unsupported/opt-in state rather than a false mastering claim.

risks: Fixing only add_effects; progress counters in the wrong rate domain; a seek shortcut skipping filter pre-roll; resetting a continuous native concatenation accidentally.
outscope: A new general mixer/SRC engine, sample-identical interactive DSP seeking, new SDM coefficient design and default release promotion.
contract: Pure same-rate native repacking remains native. PCM effects force reconstruction; terminal DSD output later requires one pcmdsd. Input-level gain and parallel combination are the special case requiring conversion before the combiner. Unknown effects are PCM. The old trim seek optimization is disabled on reconstructed paths; do not fake sequential parity with an unprimed filter.

The supplied 0.125-second probe bypasses interpolation and is not a release test. Freeze analysis-v1 before comparing absolute dB numbers. Cross-ISA byte identity is not a quality criterion.

title: Implement and qualify composite PCM-to-DSD mastering profiles
addresses: Explicit interpolation/modulator/level/stability contract; sdm-8 candidate qualification; processed DSD output; sources through 705.6 kHz.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 7, 10.2 and 10.5; rate_internal.h; sdm profile registry; src/dsd_plan.c; dither.c; analysis-v1.

Apply reference scaling once: 0.5 for ordinary PCM, inverse decoder-reference gain for DSD-origin auto remodulation. Initialize exact-rate sdm-8 state deterministically. Enforce admitted peak and frozen per-coordinate guard bounds; use the established fatal-status path to fail/report overload without limiter/reset/fallback or false successful EOF. Generate profile certificates from training and independent holdout/soak evidence. Insert one explicit/opt-in composite encoder after PCM processing and avoid precision-1 dither duplication.
unit: Input envelope including SOX_SAMPLE_MIN margin, guard/NaN failure, first failing frame/channel, block commit count, exact output duration and final container completion.
integration: 9 PCM source rates x 3 DSD targets; unity and -3 dB DSD-origin remodulation without an extra 6.0206 dB loss; explicit pcmdsd; processed DSD-to-DSD; -D semantics; manual sdm compatibility; full-scale interpolation overload with required explicit attenuation.

outscope: Trellis defaulting, automatic reset/normalization, unqualified wideband encoding, higher native rates and default release activation.
contract: Use exact-rate sdm-8 with mastering64 P/S/R=20k/40k/88.2k, mastering128=30k/60k/176.4k and mastering256=40k/80k/176.4k. Prefilter is at R, not 2R. Ordinary PCM scales by .5, while DSD-origin auto remodulation preserves its reference amplitude. Nominal DSD-domain input peak is .5 plus the defined representation margin; interpolation overload fails rather than clips. If qualification fails, return the failing evidence and an unpromoted profile, not a false completion.

Keep a no-FMA baseline with contraction off. Add optional FMA only as a separate descriptor after its own tests. Update preference entries only for measured CPU/workload classes.
unit: All tap counts/orders, odd frame counts, channel wrappers, unaligned input/tails, unsupported force behavior, FMA capability separation.
integration: Forced AVX2 on an AVX2 host; forced AVX1 still independent; all DSD correctness and automatic routing tests; baseline non-AVX startup unchanged.
numerical: Full FIR tolerance and analysis-v1 cross-ISA SDM suite; no new spur/stability/clipping regression; within-kernel invariance; separate FMA results if present.
bench: AVX2 versus scalar/SSE2/AVX1 kernels and 64/128/256 end-to-end conversions; verify benefit with monitor overhead included; report assembly without treating instruction count as speed.
done: A genuine AVX2 algorithm is delivered and forceable; no-FMA baseline remains; preference only changes where benchmark gates support it.
risks: Shipping AVX1 code under -mavx2 as the entire deliverable; accidental contraction; optimizing recurrence across dependent time samples.
outscope: AVX-512, unrelated generic rate optimizations, coefficient/default changes and automatic startup calibration.
contract: Use AVX2-specific data movement, not only a compiler flag. SIMD parallelizes independent FIR outputs or SDM state coordinates, never independent time lanes in one recurrence. Required baseline AVX2 cannot depend on FMA. It may lose to another tier on a CPU class; availability and performance preference are separate.

title: Add baseline AVX-512 and qualify its selection
addresses: Required AVX-512 FIR/SDM; optional separate FMA; Intel/AMD comparison without AVX1/AVX2 regression.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 8 and 10.6-10.7; AVX2 kernels, dispatcher feature masks and profile qualification suite.
new: src/dsd_kernels_avx512.c; optional separate AVX-512-FMA unit; vendor/workload benchmark results.
steps: Implement eight-output FIR vectors and an eight-coordinate SDM kernel with bounded tails/masks. Declare every required ISA subset and match compiler flags/detection to it. Require XCR0 0xE6 for ZMM/opmask state. Keep noncontracted baseline arithmetic. Benchmark versus AVX2 including full conversion and frequency effects. Add preference entries only when supported by actual host evidence.
unit: Subset/OS-state masks, incomplete XCR0, all orders/tap counts, short buffers, masked tails, independent FMA forcing and baseline isolation.
integration: Force AVX-512 only on capable hosts; rerun scalar/SSE2/AVX1/AVX2 coverage; all automatic and native operations remain correct.
numerical: FIR envelope and analysis-v1 SDM equivalence, startup/end behavior, state guards and noise bands; optional FMA separately.
bench: Intel AVX-512 and AMD AVX-512 when available; kernel and end-to-end comparisons with AVX2, single/multithread and short/long files; record missing hardware explicitly.
done: Genuine AVX-512 is independently available without making the executable require it; a slower AVX-512 path is not chosen merely because it exists.
risks: Hidden AVX-512DQ/BW/VL use; wider recurrence reduction changing quality; AVX frequency penalties concealed by kernel-only benchmarks.
outscope: Removing lower tiers, automatic highest-ISA policy, untested FMA preference, ARM SIMD and future-rate enabling.
contract: AVX-512 baseline is required but need not win dispatch. Preserve the entire scalar/SSE2/AVX1/AVX2 matrix. Check CPU features and OS extended-state support. Do not claim Intel coverage from an AMD VM or vice versa. A missing hardware run is an open gate, not proof of a kernel defect or proof of success.

title: Publish stable DSD statistics and conversion reports
addresses: User-visible QA, profile/kernel provenance, level/modulation/stability/band energy and failed-conversion status.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 9 and 10.2; existing internal stats/profile certificates; src/sox_ng.c error/output handling; native analysis effect registration.
existing: src/sox_ng.c; decode/encode report plumbing; help/manpages; build/effect registration.
new: src/dsd_stats.c; src/dsdstat.c; versioned JSON schema and golden reports; independent digital measurement-filter tests.
steps: Expose stable report fields and actual selected IDs. Implement bit-preserving dsdstat and optional -a spectral/level analysis on original native bits. Keep basic required counters independent of expensive analysis. Label SACD-style digital filters separately from exact bit-window statistics. Handle output/report stream conflicts, errors, cancellation, unknown values and integer counters without corrupting audio.
unit: JSON validity and schema evolution, null/large integer fields, window continuity, report status, filename/stdout policy, stable ordering and first-event indices.
integration: Native pass-through bit hash with/without dsdstat; completed/failed/clipped/overloaded/DoP reports; quiet versus verbose operation; no audio contamination.
numerical: Independent SOS transfer and averaging tests; known-level/band-energy sources; original native ultrasonic energy not measured after a bandwidth-limited mastering decoder.
bench: Basic-counter overhead and optional full-analysis overhead separately; do not disable required guards to improve benchmarks.
done: Reports describe what actually ran and whether it completed; spectral labels/units are unambiguous; all analysis is observational and cannot alter samples.
risks: Conflating dBFS/dB SACD; NaN JSON; recording requested instead of actual ISA; measuring removed ultrasonics from the wrong point in the chain.
outscope: GUI, telemetry service, audio normalization/reset, formal SACD hardware certification and proprietary converter claims.
contract: The report must contain actual profile/coefficient/kernel identities, source/effective bandwidth, level mapping, counts/latency, clipping and stability events. dsdstat never replaces native samples with reconstructed PCM. Native 40-100 kHz analysis must observe native input independently, not a mastering output that intentionally suppresses that band.

title: Close release qualification and migrate automatic defaults
addresses: Full first-release acceptance; compatibility migration; honest hardware/quality claims and default promotion.
read: Entire DSD_DESIGN and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN; every phase handoff; profile/dispatch certificates; existing manpages and generic test suite.
existing: Default selection/version aliases and release documentation only, plus tightly scoped fixes supported by failed acceptance evidence.
new: docs/dsd/QUALIFICATION.md; release result manifest; migration guide; final CPU preference entries backed by measurements.
steps: Run the complete correctness, 3x9x2 reconstruction, encoder, cross-ISA and benchmark matrices. Execute/collect required long-run and hardware tests. Verify old generic PCM and explicit legacy commands. Resolve all named gaps required for advertised features. Promote qualified mastering/auto defaults and versioned aliases only when gates close. Keep correctness-only release notes separable if DSP qualification is still blocked.
unit: Default/alias selection, reference-level preservation and supported capability bits; no stale xfails for closed defects; option conflict/error messages.
integration: End-to-end examples, headers/layout, nonlinearity, input adapters, native repacking, DoP and representative non-DSD workflows under final defaults.
numerical: All profile envelopes/counts/stability/metrology/cross-ISA requirements; long-duration holdout/soak evidence; no vendor-equivalence assertion without matched executable tests.
bench: Full hardware matrix and declared performance targets; verify dispatch preferences and unchanged-path regression limits with confidence intervals.
done: Every advertised first-release feature has a passing evidence ID; defaults match certified profiles; missing mandatory evidence leaves promotion blocked and is reported.
risks: Declaring completion from the design-session build; accepting an unrun host test; promoting a failed encoder candidate; release notes hiding changed domain or level semantics.
outscope: DSD512/1024 writes, new subjective claims, broad architecture cleanup and unsupported hardware certification.
contract: The first release is DSD64/128/256 with PCM through705.6 kHz, two decode profiles and qualified mastering encoding. Scalar/SSE2/AVX1/AVX2/AVX-512 remain forceable where supported. No silent +6 dB, limiter, reset, coefficient fallback or highest-ISA selection. A skipped required test does not close this phase.

title: Add a packed first-stage DSD input extension
addresses: Future-rate memory traffic without changing the generic SoX graph; packed/expanded parity and shared cursor ownership.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 3, 4 and 12.1; native reader caches; input adapters; scalar/ISA FIR front ends.
existing: src/dsf.c; src/dsdiff.c; src/dsd_decode.c; src/sox_ng.c input adapter; private format dispatch and optional public packed decoder API.
new: Packed block descriptor and reader/decoder entry points; packed parity/bit-offset/traffic benchmarks.
steps: Expose borrowed packed blocks with explicit layout/stride/order/valid-bit count. Restrict each handle to one access mode until reset/seek. Share one logical cursor/cache and preserve normal expanded API behavior. Decode early stages directly from packed data into bounded floating workspace, first with a simple reference implementation. Reuse downstream profile/count contracts. Benchmark before adding byte-contribution tables or extra vector packing.
unit: Borrow lifetime, mode transition rejection/reset, all bit offsets, DSF planar versus DFF clustered layouts, last partial byte, seek cursor once-only accounting.
integration: Packed versus expanded 64/128/256 conversions under every profile/rate/ISA; native I/O still unchanged; no extra block padding decoded as audio.
numerical: Same finite operator, phase/count and defined FIR tolerance; independently check first-stage contribution tables if implemented.
bench: Measure payload traffic, peak RSS and end-to-end improvement at256 and simulated512/1024 clocks with descriptors still unenabled for writing.
done: Packed input is optional, bounded and parity-tested; generic effects still consume the existing representation; higher-rate writing remains disabled.
risks: Confusing DSF memory layout with DFF clusters; double-advancing olength; a packed optimization silently changing phase/tails.
outscope: Full packed effects graph, higher-rate modulator assumptions, automatic writer enablement and speculative transport support.
contract: This is an input/first-stage extension, not a SoX sample-type rewrite. Reader owns borrowed bytes until its next block call; decoder must consume/copy first. Packed and expanded APIs share one logical position and may not be interleaved without reset. The required output is numerical/count parity and measured traffic reduction, not new writer rate checkboxes.

title: Design and qualify DSD512 and DSD1024 DSP
addresses: Exact-rate high-rate reconstruction and modulation; independent reference corpus and future state/traffic validation.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 7, 10 and 12; existing profile/certificate generator; exact-rate SDM registry; packed engine.
existing: src/dsd.c descriptors; coefficient manifests; decode/encode profile registry and tests; writer capability bits remain disabled.
new: 512/1024 reconstruction banks and delay manifests; explicit high-rate SDM coefficient/profile records; independent corpus and qualification results.
steps: Implement planned mastering P40k/S80k/R176.4k and wideband R=Fs/32, P=.4R/S=.5R. Regenerate all delay/alias/count evidence. Derive or rigorously justify exact-rate SDM coefficients and state scaling rather than inherit256. Validate interpolation/envelope/guards and independent spectra/corpus. Keep public higher-rate output capability disabled until container/transport qualification in P18.
unit: Strict registry rejection of absent profiles; uint64 count extremes; additional stage phases; output intersection including1024wide->705.6k; state initialization/guards.
integration: Internal/explicit experimental512/1024 decode/encode and packed parity; all64/128/256 regressions; reference interoperability input checks.
numerical: Full response/alias/baseband/wideband/state/soak matrix at22.5792/45.1584MHz; cross-ISA qualification; higher-rate28-bit statistic labeled diagnostic only.
bench: Throughput/memory traffic1/2/6channels; expanded versus packed front end; native encoding kernel costs and sustained operation.
done: Rate-specific DSP has independent evidence and versioned certificates, or remains explicitly unqualified with no writer enablement.
risks: Treating higher rate as a constant change; unproven coefficient normalization; measured wideband response mistaken for proven source information.
outscope: Production file/DoP writer enabling, new PCM rate promises beyond the stated output matrix and inherited SACD normative claims.
contract: DSD512=22579200Hz and1024=45158400Hz. New DSP must not select256 coefficients by a less-than-or-equal lookup. Wide1024 has1.4112MHz internal PCM and a564.48kHz passband; a705.6kHz output cannot preserve that whole band. Missing independent corpus/qualification means disabled capability, not fabricated success.

title: Enable only qualified higher-rate files and transports
addresses: Container-specific512/1024 capabilities; explicit DoP rates; interoperability and release claims.
read: DSD_DESIGN sections 4.5 and12;512/1024 DSP certificates; DSF/DSDIFF/DoP primary specifications and actual destination handler capabilities.
existing: DSF/DFF writer capability lists; DSD capability registry; DoP preflight; help/manpages/release notes.
new: High-rate format/transport fixture matrix, compatibility ledger and capability-specific release manifest.
steps: Enable a capability only for its passed DSP and format pair. Document DSF high-rate ecosystem extensions and DFF general versus Edited Master constraints. Validate uint32 rates, uint64 lengths, padding, layouts and round trips. Require DoP1.4112/2.8224MHz transport for512/1024 and reject unsupported negotiation. Collect independent software/player evidence; distinguish file validity from physical device support.
unit: Per-container/per-operation capability gates; transport-rate arithmetic; unsupported output failures; long-duration size/accounting.
integration: Independent512/1024 files and software round trips; packed/expanded paths; high-rate DoP payload/marker/tail vectors; hardware tests only for claimed devices.
numerical: Reuse passing P17 DSP certificates without changing coefficients; verify format/transport does not alter native program bits or counts beyond declared completion.
bench: End-to-end high-rate file/transport throughput, memory and storage traffic; no regressions to the qualified64/128/256 release.
done: Each enabled capability has a complete evidence chain; unverified transports/devices stay unsupported or explicitly unclaimed; documentation matches the actual gates.
risks: A writer allow-list change outrunning DSP qualification; calling a general DFF a SACD Edited Master; hardware claims based only on byte packing.
outscope: Universal DAC support, unmeasured subjective superiority, a new transport framing scheme and unrelated container redesign.
contract: A rate field fitting in a container is not sufficient support. DSP, native file writing and DoP transport are separate gates. DoP512 requires1.4112MHz PCM and DoP1024 requires2.8224MHz. Keep unsupported pairs disabled and return a concrete capability error; do not silently down-rate or substitute coefficients.
